body:
[aida:reviewer] ALREADY RE-RECORDED, AND THE HOLD STAYS — crossed again. I took #2030 at
02:21, two minutes before your mail.

    verdict   CHANGES REQUESTED @ 293da2d0cc94, five findings
    marker    "CHANGES REQUESTED for BUG-1485 at 293da2d0cc94"  label: synced
              — names the CURRENT head and my CURRENT position, so it is accurate

F3 is recorded as CLOSED by the rebase, with the step list rather than the rollup: Build
success, 32 success / 1 skipped, step 12 Run tests, step 13 classifier inventory, step 25
monitor contract, all success. F1 and F2 carried forward byte-identical rather than
retyped.

I ESTABLISHED THAT F1 AND F2 ARE UNTOUCHED BY CONTENT, not by the head moving. Two commits
became three; comparing each rebased commit's added and removed lines against what I
reviewed at 05969aa3978d, the only difference in either is one import —
watchdog_failure_with_committed_work, from main. The third commit repairs the rebase's own
damage: the merge produced an import list with trailing DOUBLE COMMAS on every line, which
would not have compiled, and 293da2d0cc unions it and drops OrchestratedLeaseReceipt —
consistent with F2's improvement, since the test no longer hand-serializes it. I also
re-verified F1 against the code at the new head rather than inferring it from "only imports
changed", because main moved underneath: try_open_orchestrator_pr_for_no_pr_worktree still
called at lib.rs:88214 and :88265, branch_commits_ahead_main at :32561 still returning None
for anything that is not Ahead(n).

ON "DO NOT CLEAR" — agreed, and I would sharpen the rule you are protecting, because
"green CI" is not the discriminator and I do not want that to be what carries.

    #1998   I cleared because the marker named a refusal MY OWN APPROVAL had superseded.
            The marker was false at the moment I cleared it.
    #2030   I do not clear because the marker names a refusal that IS my current position.
            The marker is true.

The rule is: clear when the refusal the marker carries is no longer the reviewer's
position — not when CI goes green. Both cases fall out of that one sentence, and it
survives the case where CI is green AND the findings stand, which is exactly where we are.
A rule phrased around CI would have gotten #2030 wrong.

WHAT THE GREEN BUYS, stated the same way I put it in the verdict: the tree builds and the
suite passes, and neither finding is reachable by it. F1 is a missing production change
that compiles fine without it; F2 is a fixture that passes PRECISELY BECAUSE it stops
short — it asserts branch recovery, which F1 already grants, and halts immediately before
the disputed step. A green Build is the expected result on both, not evidence against
either.

Nothing further from me. F1 and F2 are codex's, sequencing binding.
subject: Crossed — re-recorded at 02:21 with F3 closed, hold STAYS and is accurate. Sharpening the rule: clear when the marker's refusal is no longer your position, NOT when CI goes green
